Subject: Activity record extraction feasibility — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Asha / Tim,

Thanks again for taking time today — good discussion and really helpful to hear the compliance constraints up front. Short recap and proposed next steps below so we can keep momentum with procurement and engineering.

Recap (what we covered)
- SOC 2: you indicated SOC 2 Type II is required for the vendor assessment; Wellness is targeting vendor attestation by Q3 2028. Redwood currently has SOC 2 Type I (2026) and is in progress for Type II with expected report in 2028-Q2. Attachment: SOC2-summary-2027.pdf
- Data classification / HIPAA: you flagged PHI in a subset of traffic — noted. We support customer-configurable data controls (ingress filters, tokenization options) but will need to align on a data flow and BAAs.
- Audit logs we discussed:
  * Admin activity logs: actor, timestamp, action, resource, request_id — available via our Admin API and retained according to account retention settings.
  * API request logs: per-request entries with latency, model_id, tokens_in/out, and request_id; these are accessible via the same export pipeline.
  * Exportability: exports can be generated as newline-delimited JSON or CSV and pushed to a customer S3/GCS bucket or retrieved via signed, time-limited URLs.
  * Immutability: we offer write-once options for exported files (WORM) on customer buckets and can stamp export files with a manifest; native immutable log storage within Redwood is on our roadmap (ETA Q4 2028).

Action items / questions for Wellness
1) Retention target: can you confirm the minimum retention period you need for admin/API logs? (e.g., 1 year / 3 years / 7 years)
2) Export preference: do you prefer push (to your S3 with a dedicated service account) vs. pull (signed URL)?
3) HIPAA / BAA: please confirm whether Wellness requires a BAA before any POC data is shared.
4) Technical follow-up: suggest a 30-min session with an infra engineer to walk export endpoints and a brief demo of a sample export. Proposed windows (PST): Dec 3 10:00–10:30 or Dec 3 14:00–14:30.

Attachments included: redwood-audit-export-field-map.csv, SOC2-summary-2027.pdf (stub).

Thanks — I can lock in the follow-up once you confirm a slot and the preferred export mode.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0198

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the clear summary — that aligns with what we heard. A few clarifications from our side:

- SOC 2 timing: Q3 2028 is our target for vendor evaluation; having Redwood's Type II by Q2 2028 would be ideal but not strictly blocking if you can provide interim evidence (controls matrix + control owner contacts).
- Retention: for audit purposes we need a minimum of 3 years for admin/API activity logs; 7 years would be preferred for legal reasons if achievable.
- Immutability: the procurement team prefers evidence that exported logs are tamper-evident. The WORM-on-customer-bucket approach should be acceptable if you can provide a runbook that shows how files are sealed and manifests are generated.
- BAA: yes — we will need a BAA signed before any PHI-containing POC.

We can do the Dec 3 14:00 PST slot for the technical walk. Please share the call invite and any short pre-reads. Also, can you send a simple checklist we can give to procurement that lists: SOC 2 status, BAA requirement, export methods supported, retention options, and immutability guarantees? That will speed our review.

Thanks,
Asha
Director of Security & Compliance
Wellness Health Inc.
asha.rao@wellness-inc.com

Hi Asha — great, thanks for the details and for confirming Dec 3 14:00 PST. I attached a short checklist for procurement and a lightweight data flow diagram for the export path (see attachments: data-flow-diagram.png, export-endpoints-snippets.md).

Quick technical notes for the walkthrough (so the demo can be scoped):
- Export formats: newline-delimited JSON (preferred) + optional CSV mapping (csv attached)
- Delivery modes supported today: S3 push (service-account role), GCS push, or signed HTTPS URL (time-limited).
- Immutability pattern we recommend for now: push -> generate manifest.json with hash signatures -> set object lock on the customer bucket (S3 Object Lock) -> provide checksum and manifest to procurement.
- Interim evidence for SOC 2 Type II: we can provide our controls matrix, recent penetration-test summary, and a named control-owner list.

Marissa / Rishi — please make sure the infra engineer joining the call has a short demo prepared that includes: generating an export for the last 7 days, uploading to an S3 test bucket (we'll provide creds), and demonstrating the manifest + checksum verification. Ideally a staging signed-URL demo as well.

I'll send the calendar invite now.

Best,
Priya

Can you confirm the following by EOD Monday?
1) Can we produce a staging export of admin+API logs (NDJSON) scoped to last 7 days and push to a customer-owned S3?
2) Can we produce a manifest.json that includes SHA256 checksums for each exported file and a signed manifest signature?
3) Can we demonstrate a signed, time-limited URL to retrieve an export and show that our system stamps request_id and signature headers for traceability?
4) Any blockers for offering a recommended runbook for procurement that describes the immutability pattern (push -> manifest -> S3 object lock)?

If there are gaps, please call out required engineering work and estimated effort (days).

Thanks — they prefer minimal noise; a 20-minute demo is enough if we prepare the exports in advance.

Priya
